# ax-wait

A typed wait: the agent names a reference it already holds, the tool waits (polling, if it must, where the agent cannot see it) until something happens or the time limit passes, and returns what happened with the cursor that resumes the wait. The agent waits with one call instead of a polling loop of its own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ax-wait#v1.2.14
```

It installs `lib/ouro/ax/wait.ts`, with `ax-exit-codes`, `ax-outcome`. Its tests are `ax-wait-tests`. Every item runs on Node 22.18 or later as it is copied: the files import each other as `./<file>.ts`. The [Ouro AX guide](../guides/ax.md) shows how they fit together.

## Exports

### `AxEvent`

One thing that happened, with the cursor that resumes after it.

```ts
interface AxEvent {
  cursor: string;
  type: string;
  at: string;
  by: string;
  target: AxRef | null;
  summary: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### `DEFAULT_WAIT_EXITS`

The default: a satisfied or open wait exits `ok`; a wait that timed out or can no longer happen exits `error`.

```ts
const DEFAULT_WAIT_EXITS: WaitExits
```

### `formatDuration`

Milliseconds as the shortest exact duration `parseDuration` reads back: "2m", "90s", "500ms".

```ts
function formatDuration(ms: number): string
```

### `Fresh`

How current the source is, so an agent can tell "nothing happened" from "nothing was seen".

```ts
interface Fresh {
  state: string;
  asOf: string | null;
}
```

### `isWait`

Whether a value is a wait of this version (its shape only).

```ts
function isWait(v: unknown): v is Wait
```

### `parseDuration`

"90s", "2m", "1h", "500ms" or a bare number of seconds, as milliseconds; null when it is none of these.

```ts
function parseDuration(text: string): number | null
```

### `validateWait`

Checks a wait: one that can go on names how to resume it, and a satisfied one carries what happened.

```ts
function validateWait(v: unknown): Validation
```

### `wait`

Builds a wait; a `timed-out` or `waiting` wait needs `resume`, which `validateWait` checks.

```ts
function wait(fields: WaitFields): Wait
```

### `Wait`

The envelope a wait returns.

```ts
interface Wait {
  ax: typeof WAIT_VERSION;
  for: string;
  target: AxRef | null;
  state: WaitState;
  since: string;
  until: string | null;
  cursor: string | null;
  events: AxEvent[];
  fresh: Fresh | null;
  resume: NextStep | null;
  reason: string | null;
  callback: string | null;
  next: NextStep[];
}
```

### `WAIT_FLAGS`

The flags a wait command takes, shaped as `ax-command` flags: how long to wait and where to resume from. Spread them into a command's `flags`.

```ts
const WAIT_FLAGS: Readonly<{ readonly timeout: { readonly type: "string"; readonly placeholder: "<duration>"; readonly description: "How long to wait, such as \"90s\" or \"5m\"; then it exits with a resume command."; }; readonly cursor: { readonly type: "string"; readonly placeholder: "<cursor>"; readonly descript...
```

### `WAIT_STATES`

How a wait ended.
- `satisfied`: it happened; `events` holds what happened.
- `waiting`: still waiting (a stream's first line); keep reading or resume.
- `timed-out`: nothing happened in time; `resume` waits again from the same cursor.
- `gone`: what was awaited cannot happen any more (deleted, left, closed).

```ts
const WAIT_STATES: readonly ["satisfied", "waiting", "timed-out", "gone"]
```

### `WAIT_VERSION`

A typed wait: the agent names a reference it already holds, the tool waits (polling, if it must, where the agent cannot see it) until something happens or the time limit passes, and returns what happened with the cursor that resumes the wait. The agent waits with one call instead of a polling loop of its own.

```ts
const WAIT_VERSION: "wait/1"
```

### `waitExit`

The exit code a wait gives, by its state's name in the tool's table.

```ts
function waitExit(w: Wait, exits: ExitTable, names?: Readonly<Record<"gone" | "satisfied" | "waiting" | "timed-out", string>>): number
```

### `WaitExits`

Exit code names by wait state, in the tool's table.

```ts
type WaitExits = Readonly<Record<WaitState, string>>;
```

### `WaitFields`

What `wait` takes.

```ts
type WaitFields = Pick<Wait, "for" | "state" | "since"> & Partial<Omit<Wait, "ax" | "for" | "state" | "since">>;
```

### `waitFor`

Waits on a reference until a matching event, a time limit or the target is gone, reading the source as often as `intervalMs` allows, and returns the typed wait. Inside the tool, so the agent makes one call instead of a loop.

```ts
function waitFor(options: WaitForOptions): Promise<Wait>
```

### `WaitForOptions`

What `waitFor` takes.

```ts
interface WaitForOptions {
  for: string;
  target: AxRef | null;
  cursor?: string | null;
  timeoutMs: number;
  read(cursor: string | null): Promise<WaitRead>;
  match?(event: AxEvent): boolean;
  resume(cursor: string | null): NextStep;
  next?(events: readonly AxEvent[]): NextStep[];
  callback?: string | null;
  intervalMs?: number;
  now?(): number;
  sleep?(ms: number): Promise<void>;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

### `WaitRead`

What one read of the source returns: the events after the cursor, the new cursor, freshness, and whether the target is gone.

```ts
interface WaitRead {
  events: AxEvent[];
  cursor: string | null;
  fresh?: Fresh | null;
  gone?: string | null;
}
```

### `WaitState`

```ts
type WaitState = (typeof WAIT_STATES)[number];
```

### `waitText`

The wait as text: what happened (one line per event), or that nothing did, then how to resume.

```ts
function waitText(w: Wait): string
```
